item.content:encoded:
Its soft cloth absorbs blunt force attacks harmlessly, and weapons that cause damage by piercing, cutting, or ripping can easily be repaired provided SCP-492 has access to a needle and thread.

I'm gonna edit this little part because it sounds like it is referring to the weapons being repaired instead of the damage they cause

Mentally, SCP-492 possesses all of the conventional mental patterns and though processes that define human behavior.

As for this, misspelling aside (which I will also fix), I'd say that some moderate tweaks are in order as far as tone and wording. The diction doesn't fit in a scientific document of this nature, in my opinion. I'll leave the editing to someone else though, in case my interpretation or judgments are off base.

The thought that occurs to me when I read this is "yaaaaay new anthropomorphic anomaly friend!" which I personally don't mind, but the article reads in a way that seems like that was the goal from the very beginning, at the author's first conception of this idea. Like, researchers and the O5 seemed a little too eager to befriend it. Which I'm not so sure is a good thing. That said, you still have my upvote.

item.title: Re: Dimension
item.content:encoded:
No, the group is called the SCP Foundation, commonly abbreviated as "the Foundation" or less formally "the SCP", each of which can serve as noun adjuncts, although the former is less ambiguous than the latter in most cases.

"SCP" is a colloquialism used for items classed under "special containment procedures" (even if no such procedures are required in the case of a specific item) and designated "SCP-XXX". This phrase should be avoided in the text of a report.

item.title: Re: Dimension
item.content:encoded:
I always assumed life-sized (i.e normal human) given it's was originally an animatronic dummy.

Having said that, it does bring to mind several questions:
1) if he can be repaired could he also gradually be made larger?
2) Is his "body" integral to his being or is it just a kind of vessel for whatever the hell animates him?
3) How far could his body me modified away from it's normal form before he no longer animates?
4) could his conciousness/soul/essence/whatever it is be transferred to a different body? Would a head transplant onto a 400 foot tall stuffed godzilla doll work?

These are questions SCP need answers for. If it requires a series of bizzare, unethical and potentially highly hazardous experiments all the better.
